title: WhatsApp Chat System: Complete Architecture
description: Design a WhatsApp-like instant messaging system with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a WhatsApp-scale instant messaging system supporting billions of users exchanging text, photos, videos, and voice messages. The system must guarantee message delivery, show online presence and typing indicators, support group chats up to 256 participants, and operate reliably across poor network conditions with offline message queueing.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Send and receive 1:1 text messages with delivery receipts (sent, delivered, read)
Share media messages (photos, videos, voice notes) with compression and thumbnails
Real-time presence indicators: online, offline, last seen, typing... status
Group chat support with participant management and admin controls
End-to-end encryption (E2EE) for message content using Signal Protocol
Push notifications via FCM/APNS when app is backgrounded
Offline message queue: store messages locally and sync when reconnected
Message search across chat history with full-text indexing
Status updates (stories) that disappear after 24 hours
Blocked user lists and message deletion for everyone

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Sub-100ms P95 message delivery between online users
99.99% availability with graceful degradation under network partition
Store-and-forward architecture for offline users with 30-day retention
End-to-end encryption without server access to plaintext messages
Presence heartbeat every 30 seconds with stale detection after 2 minutes
Horizontal scaling to 2+ billion monthly active users
Message ordering guarantees within a chat thread
Media upload/download with resume support for large files

data.text: Build a monolithic SignalR hub in ASP.NET Core with SQL Server persistence. Use SQL Server for users, messages, and presence tables. SignalR manages real-time connections and push notifications. This validates the message delivery flow, presence logic, and media upload pipeline.

data.title: Monolith Tech Stack
data.code:
Frontend:
  - React 18 with TypeScript
  - Vite for build tooling
  - Tailwind CSS for styling
  - React Query for server state

Backend (ASP.NET Core):
  - SignalR Hub for real-time messaging
  - Minimal API for REST endpoints
  - Entity Framework Core with SQL Server
  - Azure SQL Database for messages, users, presence
  - Azure Blob Storage for media (photos, voice notes)
  - Built-in DI, logging, and health checks

Infrastructure:
  - Azure App Service with WebSockets enabled
  - Azure Redis Cache for presence and online user lists
  - Azure Service Bus for offline notification queue
  - Single database with tables: Users, Contacts, Messages, Media, Presence, Groups

data.text: At billions of messages per day, split by domain. The Message Service handles chat history and E2EE key management, Presence Service tracks online status with heartbeats, Notification Service manages push and in-app alerts, Delivery Service tracks read receipts, and User Service manages contacts and blocking.

items: Message Service: Stores and retrieves chat history per conversation with encryption metadata, handles E2EE key pre-key bundles, and emits message events to queue for delivery.
Presence Service: Tracks online/offline status via heartbeat WebSocket connections, computes last-seen timestamps, broadcasts typing indicators to active chat participants using pub/sub.
Notification Service: Sends push notifications via FCM/APNS for background messages, manages in-app notification badges, and handles silent data messages for background sync.
Delivery Service: Tracks sent/delivered/read states per message, computes unread counts, and emits read receipt events to sender devices via SignalR.
User Service: Manages contacts, profile photos, blocked users, group memberships, and phone number verification via OTP.

Key Patterns:
  - SignalR client with auto-reconnect and offline queue
  - IndexedDB for local message persistence when offline
  - Media compression before upload (Sharp in worker)
  - Optimistic UI for sent messages with rollback on failure
  - Service Worker for push notification handling

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: Chat systems are write-heavy and real-time - optimize for delivery, not queries
Separate presence (volatile, Redis) from message history (durable, Cosmos/DynamoDB)
E2EE means the server cannot read messages - design for key management carefully
Offline queueing is mandatory: store-and-forward with conflict-free resolution
Use WebSocket/SignalR for online users and push notifications for background
data.takeaway: WhatsApp is a real-time distributed system with strict consistency needs for messages and eventual consistency for presence. Separate the hot presence path from durable message history, and always design for intermittent connectivity.
